title: South Korea to check student collars, eyeglasses at university entrance exams after cheating admission
summary: South Korea will tighten checks on students taking the high-stakes national university entrance exam this week, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said, after a candidate in another test confessed to…

image.caption: South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin watches a monitor showing about the scenario of a national tax accountant exam cheating scandal, during a plenary session Monday of the education committee at the National Assembly in Seoul. (Seo Dae-yeon/Yonhap/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World

South Korea will tighten checks on students taking the high-stakes national university entrance exam this week, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said, after a candidate in another test confessed to using a hidden ​camera and AI to cheat.
Thousands more exam inspectors will be deployed than originally planned to monitor for any cheating

Authorities will place stickers ​on the buttons of candidates' clothing to cover up any miniature cameras hidden inside during the annual College Scholastic Ability Test, ​Han told a news conference on Tuesday.
"We are not trying to add burdens to you through this thorough inspection," she told students.
"It's a minimum level of protection measures ⁠to guarantee a venue for ‌fair competition."

The government ordered the crackdown ⁠after a man ⁠who got the top score in the ‌national exam for tax accountants said on Sunday he had taken photos of the questions and sent them to an AI tool, which then sent back answers to a smartphone.
South Korean Buddhists pray at the Bongeunsa Temple in Seoul on Nov. 13, 2025, for students sitting for the annual college entrance exam, known locally as Suneung. (Anthony Wallace/AFP/Getty Images)

His confession sparked a national scandal ⁠and raised questions over the credibility of national exams. The Suneung, as it is known, can dictate social mobility and career trajectories, and air traffic in the country often stops for several minutes during sections of the exam that requires active listening.
Some critics say the high stakes and the pressure to succeed have led to a negative impact on the mental health of many South Korea teens.
10-year ban on retakes for cheaters

Han said authorities will check students' collars for concealed devices and use metal detectors. Glasses worn by students will be ‌inspected to ensure that they are not smart glasses, which can be used to photograph or film material.
Cheating on exams using advanced equipment was no different from the "theft" of the hard work of other students, President Lee ​Jae Myung said in a post on X.
"If any of you are considering cheating on ⁠an exam … please abandon the idea," Lee said.

South Korea Prime Minister Prime Minister Han Seong-sook holds a televised briefing Tuesday in Seoul, in the wake of a cheating admission ahead of the country's impactful university entrance exams. (Ahn Jung-won/Yonhap/The Associated Press)
Exam participants will be required to ⁠leave bags and personal belongings in corridors outside the examination rooms.

South Korean authorities ⁠plan ⁠to seek co-operation from technology companies ​to investigate whether there is evidence that exam questions were captured and sent to ​generative AI apps during ⁠the test, Han said.

Nearly 8,400 additional exam inspectors are due to be deployed at exam sites nationwide, according to the prime minister.
The government will extend from one year to a decade a ban on retaking the exam for those caught cheating, she ⁠said.
